status: research-backed coverage map; NOT a legally reviewed policy library

questions.label: Name
questions.example: Example: Riverside Family Grill

questions.label: Mission
questions.example: Example: We serve fresh meals with friendly, consistent service.

questions.label: Values
questions.example: Example: Respect, safety, teamwork, and accountability.

questions.label: Story
questions.example: Example: Our family opened this restaurant to bring neighbors together.

questions.label: Guest Promise
questions.example: Example: Greet guests promptly and resolve concerns respectfully.

questions.label: Logo
questions.example: Example: Upload a PNG or JPG logo, or skip for now

questions.label: Locations
questions.example: Example: Memphis, Tennessee

questions.label: Languages
questions.example: Example: English and Spanish

questions.label: Employment Status
questions.example: Example: Your written offer identifies your position and employment arrangement. Direct questions to the general manager.

questions.label: Classifications
questions.example: Example: We use full-time, part-time, and seasonal positions. Your offer identifies your classification.

questions.label: Hiring
questions.example: Example: The general manager coordinates interviews and confirms offers in writing.

questions.label: Background Checks
questions.example: Example: If a position requires screening, management explains the process before requesting authorization.

questions.label: Work Authorization
questions.example: Example: The hiring manager coordinates work-authorization paperwork during onboarding.

questions.label: Orientation
questions.example: Example: New employees tour the restaurant, review safety procedures, and meet their station trainer.

questions.label: Intro Period
questions.example: Example: Your first 30 days include regular training check-ins with your manager.

questions.label: Job Descriptions
questions.example: Example: Review your job description with your manager before beginning independent work.

questions.label: Cross Training
questions.example: Example: Ask your manager about learning another station. A trainer must sign off before independent work.

questions.label: Performance Reviews
questions.example: Example: Managers meet with employees every six months to discuss performance and development.

questions.label: Promotions
questions.example: Example: Employees may discuss advancement interests with the general manager.

questions.label: Resignation
questions.example: Example: Give resignation notices to the general manager so the team can plan the transition.

questions.label: Availability
questions.example: Example: Submit availability changes to the scheduling manager before the next schedule is prepared.

questions.label: Schedule Publication
questions.example: Example: The next week's schedule is posted in the scheduling app each Thursday.

questions.label: Changes
questions.example: Example: Management communicates schedule changes directly to affected employees.

questions.label: Shift Swaps
questions.example: Example: Both employees must receive manager approval before swapping shifts.

questions.label: Call Out
questions.example: Example: Call the manager on duty as soon as you know you cannot work your shift.

questions.label: No Show
questions.example: Example: If someone misses a shift without contact, the manager attempts to reach them and reviews the circumstances.

questions.label: Timeclock
questions.example: Example: Record your start, end, and break times using the timeclock. Report missed punches to your manager.

questions.label: Off Clock Work
questions.example: Example: Record all time worked. Report any work performed outside a recorded shift to management.

questions.label: Breaks
questions.example: Example: Check with the shift manager before taking a break so your station has coverage.

questions.label: Overtime
questions.example: Example: Ask your manager before working beyond your scheduled hours. Record all hours actually worked.

questions.label: Split Shifts
questions.example: Example: The scheduling manager discusses split-shift assignments with affected employees.

questions.label: On Call
questions.example: Example: Any on-call assignment must be communicated by the scheduling manager.

questions.label: Weather Closures
questions.example: Example: Check the staff communication channel for closure updates and contact the manager if travel is unsafe.

questions.label: Payday
questions.example: Example: Payday is every other Friday. Contact payroll with questions about your pay statement.

questions.label: Direct Deposit
questions.example: Example: Ask payroll for the available payment methods and the forms needed to set up your choice.

questions.label: Wage Notices
questions.example: Example: Payroll provides written pay information during onboarding and communicates approved changes.

questions.label: Tips
questions.example: Example: Report tips through the restaurant's approved payroll process.

questions.label: Tip Credit
questions.example: Example: Ask payroll for the restaurant's written tip-credit arrangement before accepting a tipped assignment.

questions.label: Tip Pools
questions.example: Example: Management provides the written tip-sharing arrangement to participating employees for review.

questions.label: Service Charges
questions.example: Example: Management explains how service charges are recorded and distributed before an event.

questions.label: Automatic Gratuity
questions.example: Example: Use only manager-approved automatic gratuities and explain them clearly to guests.

questions.label: Credit Card Tips
questions.example: Example: Credit-card tips are reconciled against the POS report and processed through payroll.

questions.label: Dual Jobs
questions.example: Example: Record the role worked when moving between tipped and non-tipped assignments.

questions.label: Cash Shortages
questions.example: Example: Report a cash shortage to the manager for review. Do not adjust another employee's drawer.

questions.label: Deductions
questions.example: Example: Ask payroll to explain any deduction that you do not understand.

questions.label: Bonuses
questions.example: Example: Any bonus arrangement is documented separately and explained before the measurement period.

questions.label: Employee Meals
questions.example: Example: Ask the shift manager before ordering your employee meal and enter it through the POS.

questions.label: Discounts
questions.example: Example: Employee discounts require manager approval and must be entered using the correct POS code.

questions.label: Insurance
questions.example: Example: Ask the benefits coordinator for current plan documents and eligibility information.

questions.label: Pto
questions.example: Example: Submit paid-time-off requests through the scheduling app for review.

questions.label: Holidays
questions.example: Example: The holiday schedule is communicated in advance by management.

questions.label: Respect
questions.example: Example: Treat coworkers and guests with respect, including during busy or difficult shifts.

questions.label: Harassment
questions.example: Example: Report harassment concerns to the general manager or the owner.

questions.label: Complaints
questions.example: Example: Raise workplace concerns with the general manager in person or through the designated contact channel.

questions.label: Alternate Reporting
questions.example: Example: If your concern involves your manager, contact the owner directly.

questions.label: Nonretaliation
questions.example: Example: Employees may raise concerns without retaliation. Report suspected retaliation to the owner.

questions.label: Investigation
questions.example: Example: Management reviews concerns promptly and asks employees to provide accurate information.

questions.label: Confidentiality
questions.example: Example: Protect guest payment details and private business records. Ask management if you are unsure what may be shared.

questions.label: Conflicts
questions.example: Example: Disclose outside business relationships that could affect purchasing or management decisions.

questions.label: Dating
questions.example: Example: Discuss personal relationships that create a reporting-line conflict with the owner.

questions.label: Social Media
questions.example: Example: Only authorized staff may publish posts on the restaurant's official accounts.

questions.label: Phones
questions.example: Example: Keep personal phones stored during active service unless your manager approves their use.

questions.label: Privacy
questions.example: Example: Ask management how employee records are stored and who may access them.

questions.label: Surveillance
questions.example: Example: Management explains camera locations and recording practices during orientation.

questions.label: Cash Handling
questions.example: Example: Use your assigned register login and count your drawer with a manager.

questions.label: Theft
questions.example: Example: Report suspected theft to management without confronting another person.

questions.label: Discipline
questions.example: Example: Management reviews the facts and explains any corrective action directly to the employee.

questions.label: Appeals
questions.example: Example: Employees may ask the owner to review a disputed management decision.

questions.label: Illness Reporting
questions.example: Example: Tell the manager before your shift if you are ill or have symptoms that could affect food safety.

questions.label: Exclusion
questions.example: Example: The manager determines work restrictions using the restaurant's approved illness procedures.

questions.label: Allergens
questions.example: Example: Refer ingredient and allergy questions to the manager or designated kitchen lead.

questions.label: Cross Contact
questions.example: Example: Use the approved clean tools and preparation area for an allergy order.

questions.label: Handwashing
questions.example: Example: Follow posted handwashing procedures before handling food and after contamination.

questions.label: Sanitation
questions.example: Example: Complete your station cleaning checklist and report missing sanitation supplies.

questions.label: Temperature Control
questions.example: Example: Use the station temperature log and report readings outside the posted limits.

questions.label: Chemical Safety
questions.example: Example: Keep chemicals labeled and stored away from food. Consult the safety sheet before use.

questions.label: Slips
questions.example: Example: Mark wet floors and clean spills promptly when it is safe to do so.

questions.label: Burns
questions.example: Example: Use dry protective mitts for hot cookware and warn coworkers when carrying hot items.

questions.label: Cuts
questions.example: Example: Report cuts promptly and follow the first-aid and food-handling procedures.

questions.label: Knife Use
questions.example: Example: Carry knives safely and store them in the designated rack after cleaning.

questions.label: Equipment
questions.example: Example: Operate equipment only after station training and manager authorization.

questions.label: Injury Reporting
questions.example: Example: Report injuries and near misses to the manager immediately.

questions.label: Workers Comp
questions.example: Example: Ask the general manager for the injury-reporting and workers' compensation contact information.

questions.label: Fire
questions.example: Example: Raise the alarm and follow the posted fire evacuation plan.

questions.label: Severe Weather
questions.example: Example: Follow the manager's directions and move to the designated shelter area when instructed.

questions.label: Violence
questions.example: Example: Move away from threatening behavior and notify management or emergency services as appropriate.

questions.label: Active Threat
questions.example: Example: Follow the restaurant's emergency response training and contact emergency services when safe.

questions.label: Evacuation
questions.example: Example: Use the nearest safe exit and meet at the posted assembly point.

questions.label: Power Outage
questions.example: Example: Notify management and follow the approved food-protection and shutdown procedures.

questions.label: Service Standards
questions.example: Example: Greet arriving guests promptly and check back after food is served.

questions.label: Complaints
questions.example: Example: Listen without arguing, thank the guest, and involve a manager when resolution exceeds your authority.

questions.label: Refunds
questions.example: Example: A manager must approve refunds and record the reason in the POS.

questions.label: Comps
questions.example: Example: Managers authorize complimentary items and record the reason.

questions.label: Voids
questions.example: Example: Ask a manager to approve voids and explain the correction needed.

questions.label: Reservations
questions.example: Example: Confirm reservation details and communicate special requests to the shift lead.

questions.label: Takeout
questions.example: Example: Check items against the receipt, label the order, and verify the guest name at pickup.

questions.label: Delivery
questions.example: Example: Check packaging and order details before handing an order to a delivery driver.

questions.label: Cash Register
questions.example: Example: Use your own POS login and ask a manager about transaction errors.

questions.label: Lost Found
questions.example: Example: Give found property to the manager and record where it was found.

questions.label: Accessibility
questions.example: Example: Ask guests how you can help and involve management when an accessibility concern arises.

questions.label: Service Animals
questions.example: Example: Refer service-animal questions to the manager and treat the guest respectfully.

questions.label: Guest Privacy
questions.example: Example: Do not share guest contact or payment information outside authorized work tasks.

questions.label: Guest Allergies
questions.example: Example: Notify the kitchen lead of allergy requests and confirm the approved preparation process.

questions.label: Dress Code
questions.example: Example: Wear a clean company shirt, dark pants, and slip-resistant shoes.

questions.label: Grooming
questions.example: Example: Arrive clean and ready for food-service work. Follow station hygiene requirements.

questions.label: Hair Restraints
questions.example: Example: Wear the hair restraint designated for your station.

questions.label: Jewelry
questions.example: Example: Follow the posted station rules for jewelry while handling food.

questions.label: Footwear
questions.example: Example: Wear closed-toe, slip-resistant shoes suitable for kitchen floors.

questions.label: Uniform Issued
questions.example: Example: Management issues two uniform shirts during orientation.

questions.label: Uniform Care
questions.example: Example: Keep uniforms clean and report damage to your manager.

questions.label: Uniform Return
questions.example: Example: Return issued uniforms to the general manager when employment ends.

questions.label: Religious Accommodation
questions.example: Example: Discuss religious dress or grooming needs with the general manager.

questions.label: Sick Leave
questions.example: Example: Contact the manager when illness affects your shift and ask about available sick leave.

questions.label: Family Leave
questions.example: Example: Ask the general manager for the family-leave request process and applicable eligibility information.

questions.label: Military Leave
questions.example: Example: Notify management when military duties affect your schedule and request leave information.

questions.label: Jury Duty
questions.example: Example: Notify management when you receive a jury summons and share scheduling information.

questions.label: Bereavement
questions.example: Example: Contact the general manager to discuss leave following a bereavement.

questions.label: Pregnancy Accommodation
questions.example: Example: Discuss pregnancy-related work adjustments with the general manager.

questions.label: Disability Accommodation
questions.example: Example: Request disability-related work adjustments through the general manager.

questions.label: Religious Accommodation
questions.example: Example: Discuss religious scheduling or workplace accommodation requests with the general manager.

questions.label: Lactation
questions.example: Example: Contact management to arrange the designated lactation space and break coverage.

questions.label: Protected Concerted Activity
questions.example: Example: Bring questions about workplace discussions or group concerns to management for review without retaliation.

questions.label: Whistleblowing
questions.example: Example: Report suspected wrongdoing to the owner or the relevant reporting channel.

questions.label: Licensed
questions.example: Example: Only authorized staff may serve alcohol in the restaurant's licensed service areas.

questions.label: Age Verification
questions.example: Example: Check identification using the restaurant's approved age-verification procedure.

questions.label: Server Certification
questions.example: Example: Provide required server-training documentation to management before alcohol-service assignments.

questions.label: Intoxication
questions.example: Example: Notify the manager when a guest shows signs of intoxication.

questions.label: Refusal
questions.example: Example: Involve the manager when alcohol service must be refused.

questions.label: Incident Reporting
questions.example: Example: Record alcohol-service incidents in the manager's incident log.

questions.label: Employee Consumption
questions.example: Example: Employees may not consume alcohol while working.

questions.label: Alcohol Storage
questions.example: Example: Keep alcohol in the designated secure storage areas.

questions.label: Corkage
questions.example: Example: Ask a manager before accepting guest-supplied wine or applying a corkage charge.

questions.label: Tastings
questions.example: Example: Only designated staff may conduct approved product tastings.

questions.label: Minors Employed
questions.example: Example: Management reviews age and school commitments before assigning work to student employees.

questions.label: Age Verification
questions.example: Example: The hiring manager verifies an employee's age and any required documentation before assignments are made.

questions.label: Restricted Equipment
questions.example: Example: Managers assign equipment duties only after checking age restrictions and training records.

questions.label: Restricted Hours
questions.example: Example: The scheduling manager checks applicable work-hour restrictions before publishing student schedules.

questions.label: School Schedules
questions.example: Example: Provide class schedules and exam commitments to the scheduling manager.

questions.label: Delivery Driving
questions.example: Example: Delivery-driving assignments require management review of age, licensing, and insurance requirements.

questions.label: Supervision
questions.example: Example: Student employees have a designated shift supervisor for questions and support.

questions.label: Food Truck
questions.example: Example: Complete the food-truck opening checklist before leaving the commissary.

questions.label: Commissary
questions.example: Example: Record commissary pickups and returns on the transfer log.

questions.label: Catering
questions.example: Example: The catering lead confirms transport, setup, and service assignments before departure.

questions.label: Banquets
questions.example: Example: Review the event order with the banquet captain before guests arrive.

questions.label: Buffet
questions.example: Example: Follow the buffet replenishment and temperature-check schedule.

questions.label: Self Service
questions.example: Example: Keep self-service stations stocked and report spills promptly.

questions.label: Drive Thru
questions.example: Example: Confirm each order and payment before handing food through the window.

questions.label: Ghost Kitchen
questions.example: Example: Check order names and pickup shelves carefully when working across virtual brands.

questions.label: Third Party Delivery
questions.example: Example: Verify the order number before releasing food to a third-party courier.

questions.label: Hotel Room Service
questions.example: Example: Confirm the room number and delivery instructions before leaving the service area.

questions.label: Bakery
questions.example: Example: Follow production sheets and label bakery items with preparation details.

questions.label: Coffee
questions.example: Example: Follow the beverage recipe cards and clean the espresso station between tasks.

questions.label: Bar
questions.example: Example: Complete the bar opening checklist and reconcile stock with the shift lead.

questions.label: Late Night
questions.example: Example: Use the closing safety check and designated departure procedure after late shifts.

questions.label: Seasonal
questions.example: Example: Management communicates seasonal opening and closing assignments in advance.

questions.label: Multi Location
questions.example: Example: Confirm your assigned location and reporting manager before each shift.

questions.label: Franchise
questions.example: Example: Follow the current approved brand standards supplied by management.

questions.label: Union
questions.example: Example: Direct questions about union representation to the designated representative or management contact.

questions.label: Collective Bargaining
questions.example: Example: Consult the applicable collective bargaining agreement and designated representative for covered terms.

questions.label: Multilingual Staff
questions.example: Example: Ask management for language support when training instructions are unclear.

questions.label: Shared Tips
questions.example: Example: Review the written tip-sharing arrangement with management before participating.

questions.label: Live Music
questions.example: Example: Keep exits clear during performances and direct performer questions to the event lead.

questions.label: Security
questions.example: Example: Notify the designated security lead of threats or unsafe guest behavior.

questions.label: Cashless
questions.example: Example: Explain accepted payment methods before taking an order when a guest asks about cash.

questions.label: Outdoor Dining
questions.example: Example: Check outdoor furniture and weather conditions before opening patio service.

questions.label: Final Pay
questions.example: Example: Contact payroll for the timing and delivery method of final pay.

questions.label: Property Return
questions.example: Example: Return keys, access cards, and equipment to the general manager.

questions.label: Uniform Return
questions.example: Example: Return issued uniforms to the general manager at separation.

questions.label: Access Removal
questions.example: Example: Management closes system access when an employee leaves.

questions.label: References
questions.example: Example: Refer employment-reference requests to the general manager.

questions.label: Handbook Receipt
questions.example: Example: I acknowledge receiving this handbook and know whom to contact with questions.

questions.label: Policy Acknowledgment
questions.example: Example: I acknowledge reviewing the policies supplied in this handbook.

questions.label: Training Acknowledgment
questions.example: Example: Station training completion is recorded separately by the trainer.

questions.label: Revision Acknowledgment
questions.example: Example: Management provides revised policies and requests acknowledgment of receipt.

navigation.description: Every standard and specialty section remains discoverable. Customers may skip optional entries or entire optional sections. Show relevance guidance, not hidden options.
sectionActions: Skip remaining optional entries for now
navigation.legalGate: Legal-critical data is requested only when a specific legally sensitive output requires it. Missing data does not block saving or draft preview; affected final content is marked incomplete.

skipSemantics.deferred: Skip for now adds the question to a final Review Later queue. Preserve section and question context and provide a one-click return.
skipSemantics.excluded: Skip altogether explicitly excludes the question from the final Review Later queue and omits its unanswered policy from the handbook. It remains reversible from the complete question catalog.
skipSemantics.answered: Answered questions are neither deferred nor excluded.
skipSemantics.legal: Legal-critical questions cannot be excluded when needed to finalize affected legal-sensitive policies. Allow draft progress and explain unresolved requirements.

finalReview.title: Finish Your Handbook — Questions to Revisit
finalReview.includes: All and only Skip for now questions that remain unanswered, grouped by section
finalReview.gate: Review queue is separate from legal completeness checks and payment.
